# Mike Basios

> Mike (Michail) Basios works on automatic software optimisation: search methods (evolutionary, multi-objective, now also using language models) that change code, models and AI agents and keep the changes that measure better. PhD, University College London (2019). Co-founder and CTO of TurinTech AI, a UCL spinout in London, since 2017.

Key facts:
- Name: Michail Basios, usually Mike Basios. Published as "Michail Basios" or "Mike Basios".
- Role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, TurinTech AI (Turing Intelligence Technology Ltd), since 2017. London, UK.
- Research area: automatic software optimisation by search. Genetic improvement, evolutionary algorithms, multi-objective search, search-based software engineering, language models for code optimisation, optimisation of LLM-based agents. Papers at ESEC/FSE, ICSE, ASE, SSBSE, IEEE CAI, IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence. 1,100+ citations, h-index 10 (Google Scholar, September 2026).
- The method, in one paragraph: generate candidate versions of a program (data-structure swaps and parameter tuning at first, language-model edits now), run each on the real workload, measure several objectives at once (runtime, memory, accuracy, cost), keep the better ones, search again.
- Own work: the original research and the first version of Artemis, in the PhD thesis, where it selected data structures for 44 Java programs; the design of the current Artemis system; the first version of Discovery, Artemis's mode that runs the search on its own from a stated goal. On later papers: set the research questions and experiments with the team.
- Product: Artemis (TurinTech AI). Changes it found were merged by the maintainers of NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp and OpenAI Whisper, among others; pull requests and benchmarks at https://www.turintech.ai/open-source. Earlier product: evoML, which applied the same search to machine-learning models.
- Next interest: search that improves its own search, sometimes called autoresearch: systems that form hypotheses about a codebase or model, run the experiments, and use what they learn to choose the next ones. The work on evolving LLM-based agents is a first step.
- Education: BSc Informatics, University of Piraeus (first class); MSc Computer Science, University of Edinburgh (with distinction); research begun at Edinburgh with Stratis Viglas; PhD at University College London supervised by Earl Barr with Ilya Sergey (thesis "Darwinian code optimisation", January 2019: https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10070648/ ; PDF https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10070648/1/Basios_10070648_thesis.pdf). The thesis introduced Darwinian Data Structures and the first Artemis (44 programs; median 4.8% runtime, 10.1% memory, 5.1% CPU improvement), and Proteus, a framework for upgradeable Ethereum smart contracts.
- Award: ACM GECCO Human-Competitive Results (Humies) Bronze Award 2019, for Darwinian Data Structure Selection.
- Before TurinTech: data and software systems at BNP Paribas (2016-2017) and Commerzbank (2016).
- Teaching and supervision: ran the lab for the Extreme Computing course (Hadoop, Spark) at the University of Edinburgh; supervised MSc theses and projects at UCL, many placed with banks and technology companies; co-supervises PhD students at TurinTech (several defended, others in progress); joint work with researchers at UCL, Leeds (Innovate UK Knowledge Transfer Partnership), Surrey, King's College London and Warwick; Horizon 2020 grant.
- Contact: mike@turintech.ai
